Fig. 4.1 is a world map titled 'World - Major Regions of Primary activities'. Its index has five classes: Agriculture (green), Animal husbandry (tan), Fishing (blue bands along coasts and over banks), Mining (pink stars) and Lumbering (orange log symbols). Latitude lines are marked at 60 degrees N, 30 degrees N, 0, 30 degrees S and 60 degrees S. Named on it are the Okhotsk Sea, Dogger Bank, Grand Bank, Sable Bank and Georges Bank; the continents North America, South America, Europe, Africa, Asia, Australia and Antarctica; and the Arctic, Pacific, Atlantic, Indian and Southern Oceans.

What the map shows: green agriculture over eastern North America, most of Europe, south and east Asia, parts of eastern and southern Africa, eastern South America and the coastal margins of Australia. Tan animal husbandry over the interior of North America, central and western Asia, the interior of South America, the interior and east of Australia, and the belt south of the Sahara. Blue fishing bands off north-west Europe, off the north-east coast of North America over the Grand, Sable and Georges Banks, across the north-west Pacific around the Okhotsk Sea and the coasts of Japan and China, off the west coast of South America, off the west coast of Africa, and around south-east Australia. Pink mining stars scattered across every continent except Antarctica, and also offshore in the seas. Orange lumbering symbols in a broad belt across the far north of North America, Europe and Asia, with scattered symbols in the tropics of South America, Africa, South East Asia and Australia. Antarctica carries no symbol of any kind.

Complete the chain by matching each set of characteristics in column B with its type of agriculture in column C.

| Characteristics (B) | Type of Agriculture (C) |
|---|---|
| 1) Small land holding. Maximum yield from small land. Food crops are dominant. Manual labour and use of animals. China, India, Japan, Korea, Sri Lanka and East Asian countries. Rice is the major crop. | A) Shifting Agriculture |
| 2) Large size of farm. Capital intensive, more use of modern machinery. Monoculture. Use of machinery from sowing to harvesting. Cultivation and commercial animal husbandry is done together. Per hectare low but per capita income is high. Temperate grassland, Steppes, Praries, Downs, Pampas, Velds. Wheat and maize are the major crops. | B) Horticulture |
| 3) Large farm size. Capital intensive. Monoculture. Local labour is employed. Crop is well managed for quality and processing. Per hectare yield low but total production is high. Once plantation is done, it gives production for 10 to 15 years. Tea, coffee, rubber, cocoa etc., spice plantations in Kerala, cashewnut plantation in Konkan region. Malaysia, India, Sri Lanka, Brazil, Indonesia, Caribbean Islands, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam. | C) Market Gardening |
| 4) Forest land is burnt and used for agriculture. Very small farm size. Production is very less. Production can be taken for only 2-3 years. Land left fallow and move ahead looking for another land. Forest resources decline and soil erosion occurs. Mainly practiced in forested tropical regions of Asia, South-East Asia, South and Central America and Africa. | D) Intensive Subsistence Agriculture |
| 5) Modern type of agriculture. Fulfill the demands of urban people, it is developed in fringe areas. Maximum production from limited agriculture area. Use of capital is high. Along with use of manual labour, use of scientific technology, knowledge and capital. Organic and chemical manures or fertilizers and irrigation. Practised in areas lying at distance of an overnight journey by trucks. Vegetables, fruits, milk, eggs, meat, fish etc. Developed mainly in highly industrialised and densely populated urban areas, e.g. fruits, vegetables and flowers from Khedshivapur, Saswad are brought to Pune. | E) Plantation Agriculture |
| 6) Fruits, flowers, medicinal plants, ornamental plants etc. are produced for commercial use. Use of manual labour and mechanization. Practiced in tropical, Mediterranean and temperate regions where climate is supportive. | F) Extensive Commercial Agriculture |
